title: TLR‑RICE: Token‑Latency‑Reliability augmented RICE for infrastructure-aware roadmap prioritization
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: Our current RICE-based prioritization surface (Reach/Impact/Confidence/Effort) is model-agnostic and does not account for inference-specific economics and reliability risk. That leads to biases: features that improve developer experience but materially increase token cost, or features that improve tail-latency at high infra cost, are evaluated on the same axis as purely product-facing changes.

Proposal: Adopt TLR‑RICE — an augmented scoring approach that preserves the familiarity of RICE but applies three infrastructure-aware multipliers: Token Sensitivity (T), Latency Weight (L), and Reliability Risk (R). These multipliers encode business priorities (unit economics, SLOs, and risk tolerance) and can be tuned per-customer segment (e.g., PLG vs enterprise/Dedicated).

Core idea: Compute a baseline RICE score (using Reach in thousands or other normalized unit), then multiply by three dimension factors: TokenFactor (T), LatencyFactor (L), ReliabilityFactor (R). FinalScore = RICE * TokenFactor * LatencyFactor * ReliabilityFactor.

When to use: This becomes the default scoring for roadmap candidates that touch runtime, costing levers (batching, quantization, caching), SLO/latency surfaced features, Dedicated/Private capacity changes, and any cross-cutting infra features that alter unit economics or reliability surface. For purely product UX work with no infra impact, multipliers default to 1.

Why: - Keeps PM/Execs familiar with RICE but introduces explainable adjustments for infra trade-offs. - Makes token cost and latency explicitly visible in prioritization decisions. - Enables segment-level prioritization by adjusting multipliers per customer tier.

Implementation notes: - Provide a short reference sheet and an Airtable/Sheets template so PMs can compute FinalScore. - Expose recommended multiplier defaults: TokenFactor ranges 0.6-1.4; LatencyFactor ranges 0.7-1.5; ReliabilityFactor ranges 0.6-1.6. Multipliers are descriptive and require a short justification when non-default. - Integrate with quarterly roadmap reviews and our cycle planning rubric.

This ticket documents the framework, sample scoring, acceptance criteria, documentation updates, and rollout plan.
scoring_example:
Baseline RICE formula: RICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort. Use Reach in 'thousands of requests or users impacted' to keep magnitudes reasonable.

Example A — Auto-prefix KV caching for embeddings (infra + cost reduction):
- Reach: 40 (thousands of calls/month)
- Impact: 3 (medium uplift in success rate and cost reduction)
- Confidence: 0.7
- Effort: 8 (engineering points)
Baseline RICE = (40 * 3 * 0.7) / 8 = 10.5
Assessed multipliers: TokenFactor = 1.2 (high token-savings potential), LatencyFactor = 1.1 (improves p50), ReliabilityFactor = 1.0
FinalScore = 10.5 * 1.2 * 1.1 * 1.0 = 13.86

Example B — Per-route latency SLOs + fallback routing (enterprise SLA feature):
- Reach: 8 (thousands of routes/customers enabled initially)
- Impact: 4 (high reduction in outages/incident MTTR)
- Confidence: 0.8
- Effort: 13
Baseline RICE = (8 * 4 * 0.8) / 13 = 1.97
Assessed multipliers: TokenFactor = 1.0, LatencyFactor = 1.5 (SLAs are a high priority), ReliabilityFactor = 1.4 (directly reduces outage risk)
FinalScore = 1.97 * 1.0 * 1.5 * 1.4 = 4.13

Interpretation: Even with a low baseline Reach, the enterprise SLO work rises above infra-proportional work when latency and reliability multipliers reflect customer priorities. Use thresholds for prioritization buckets (Top 10% / Next 25% / Backlog).
acceptance_criteria:
- Framework documented in Confluence with formula, multiplier guidance, and worked examples.
- One-pager summary shared to PM & Eng leads and discussed in roadmap sync.
- Spreadsheet template with computed FinalScore and fields for multiplier justification.
- At least 6 candidate roadmap items re-scored using TLR-RICE for the next cycle and results reviewed with Exec.
- Multipliers and defaults stored in the Roadmap Prioritization playbook.
- Feedback loop defined: post-release unit-economics and latency deltas feed back into multiplier calibration.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (1 week): Finalize document + examples; circulate to PMs, Eng leads, and Solutions; gather quick feedback.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Re-score open candidates for next two cycles; surface results in roadmap working group.
Phase 3 (ongoing): Use TLR-RICE for all infra-related candidates. Revisit multiplier defaults every quarter once we have telemetry.
Dependencies: decision from Eng leadership on how to normalize Reach (calls vs users), and access to token-cost model dashboard (ENG-2748).
metrics_to_track: Change in prioritized infra work acceptance (count)
Median token cost delta for shipped items
p50/p95 latency deltas for affected models
Number of enterprise SLA tickets prevented (estimated)
Correlation between predicted vs actual unit-economics improvement
